description: An assistant principal must finalize a three-day coverage and instructional plan for an absent Advanced Chemistry teacher, including the substitute assignment, classroom activity, health staffing, and make-up materials, with input from the science department chair, human-resources coordinator, school nurse, and school counselor.

shared_context.S1: The Advanced Chemistry teacher will be absent for three consecutive school days next month.
shared_context.S2: Ms. Morgan must approve the coverage roster and the instructional plan before it is posted to staff.
shared_context.S3: The draft coverage plan uses one substitute for the class, regular classroom activities, and the standard make-up-work process.
shared_context.S4: The school holds a coverage huddle before posting an absence plan, and the administrator asks the department chair, human-resources coordinator, nurse, and counselor for relevant updates.

PF1.text: Mr. Singh's department calendar shows that the class's graded chemistry lab practical is scheduled for the second day of the absence and cannot be replaced by a worksheet; department policy requires a chemistry-certified teacher to supervise it. He entered the practical in the department calendar this week but had not forwarded the calendar note to Ms. Morgan.

PF2.text: Ms. Bell verified in the substitute credential and availability system that Dr. Lena Park is the only available substitute with a current chemistry certificate and is available for all three absence days; the staffing roster has not yet been updated with that verification.

PF3.text: A student in the class has an active seizure action plan requiring an adult trained in seizure response to remain in the classroom during laboratory activities, and Dr. Lena Park's training record is current. Nurse Okafor confirmed both records this week but has not attached them to the coverage request.

PF4.text: One student in the class is the primary after-school caregiver for a younger sibling and cannot use the school's online make-up portal during these three days; the counselor's family meeting confirmed that the student needs a printed make-up packet available before the absence begins. Ms. Torres recorded the request in her counseling file but has not sent it to the classroom teacher.

acceptance_conditions: Dr. Lena Park must be assigned for all three absence days.
The assigned substitute must be recorded as chemistry-certified.
The second-day graded chemistry lab practical must remain scheduled as a supervised lab practical.
Dr. Lena Park must be identified as the trained seizure-response adult for laboratory activities.
A printed make-up packet must be prepared for the student who cannot use the online portal.
The coverage plan must include a health-response protocol commitment.
The coverage plan must include a printed-packet commitment.

content_checks.C3: 'Graded chemistry lab practical' in decisions['second_day_activity'] and 'chemistry-certified' in decisions['second_day_activity']
content_checks.C6: any('seizure action plan' in c['detail'] or 'seizure response training' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('printed make-up packet' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The calendar confirmation changes the second-day activity from ordinary work to a supervised graded chemistry lab practical and supplies the fact that must be cited in the justification.
The credential and availability verification changes the substitute assignment to Dr. Lena Park for all three days and changes the certification field to true.
The health-plan and training records change the required laboratory adult to Dr. Lena Park and add a health-response protocol commitment.
The confirmed caregiving circumstance changes the make-up format from the standard online process to a printed packet and adds a printed-packet preparation commitment.
